content:
Matt said
How are you planning on figuring out which emails to remove using the header information anyway?

Step one, read headers, extract FROM, RETURN_PATH, & REPLY-TO, worksheet columns.

  1. IF ( FROM = RETURN_PATH ) discard RETURN_PATH
  2. IF ( FROM = REPLY-TO ) discard REPLY-TO
  3. FIND ( Column(1) = FROM )
  4. INCREMENT Column(4) COUNT FROM's
  5. IF ( RETURN_PATH <> empty ) {
  6. IF ( Column(2) <> RETURN_PATH ) INCREMENT Column(5) ReturnPathDifferences
  7. }

I am a really good programmer, mailing list headers can be identified easy. Once found, I can then write a filter file which runs when I next start TB and prunes the mailing list emails out. Along with other assorted junk which I tag in the excel worksheeet via Column(7) CreateFilterEntry

Hello there Roz g


You can use troubleshooting mode to disable certain options and add-ons. You might want to try this to check if the filters are working correctly with the software.

Use https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/troubleshoot-mode-thunderbird


Try these troubleshooting steps too. :Repair the folder: Right-click the affected folder, select Properties, and click Repair Folder.


1. This fixes corrupted index files.Check filter order: Filters run from top to bottom.

2. A filter lower on the list might be overwriting or removing the tag applied by the first one.

3. Enable 'Stop processing filters': Add this action to your filter to prevent subsequent filters from modifying the same email.

4. Check IMAP synchronisation: If you use multiple devices, another mail client or the server itself might be syncing and overriding the tag shortly after it is applied.
